sentences.text: On Halvern-Faces 256×256, Sablewing is substantially more efficient than the 50-step Ordell-DDS teacher, requiring 0.94 TFLOPs per image and 8 NFE versus 5.40 TFLOPs and 50 NFE, at the cost of a higher FID (7.8 vs 7.1).
Compared with the 10-step truncated teacher (Ordell-DDS-10), Sablewing is both more efficient (0.94 vs 1.08 TFLOPs; 8 vs 10 NFE) and achieves a lower FID (7.8 vs 15.6).

Thus, Sablewing's sample quality is worse than the full 50-step teacher but better than the 10-step truncated baseline, indicating a quality cost relative to the full teacher and a quality gain over the truncated baseline; no statistical tests were reported, so these FID differences are descriptive only.
